## Covering Materials – Technical Requirements

### MRWA Code of Practice (May 2025)

**Section 6.4.1, Page 57**

| Material | Permitted? | Reason |
|----------|-----------|--------|
| **Black plastic** | ❌ **FORBIDDEN** | Causes permanent damage within 24 hours |
| **Plastic materials** | ⚠️ **Use with caution** | Can cause damage from moisture/sunlight |
| **Approved sign covers** | ✅ Yes | Must comply with Main Roads Specification 601 |
| **Hessian/cloth covers** | ✅ Yes | Must not retain moisture |

> **Important:** Using incorrect covering materials can result in permanent damage to signage, requiring costly replacement. Always refer to Main Roads Specification 601 for approved covering methods.

---

## Summary Table

| Question | Answer | Citation |
|----------|--------|----------|
| **Can I cover a nearby worksite's signage?** | Only with **coordination and agreement** – not unilaterally | MRWA COP Section 2, Page 20 |
| **What if their signs conflict with mine?** | **Coordinate first** – agree on which signs need adjustment | MRWA COP Section 6.4.1, Page 57 |
| **Do I need their permission?** | **YES** – covering another party's traffic control devices without agreement could breach the Code | MRWA COP Section 3, Page 24 |
| **What if they've finished but signs remain?** | You may cover/remove as "inappropriate to the situation" | AS 1742.3 Clause 4.2.5 |
| **What if my worksite was approved first?** | Still requires coordination – approval order doesn't override coordination requirements | MRWA COP Section 2, Page 20 |
| **What covering materials can I use?** | Approved materials only – NO black plastic | MRWA COP Section 6.4.1, Page 57 |
| **What WHS duties apply?** | Section 46 requires consultation, cooperation and coordination with other duty holders | WHS Act 2020 Section 46 |

## Consequences of Non-Compliance

| Breach | Potential Consequence |
|--------|---------------------|
| **Covering signs without authority** | Breach of MRWA COP, potential prosecution under Road Traffic Code |
| **No coordination with adjacent worksite** | TMP approval may be withheld or revoked |
| **Using incorrect covering materials** | Liability for damage to signage, potential WHS breach |
| **Interfering with active worksite TMP** | Civil liability, potential prosecution, WHS breach |

---

> **Key Rule:** Under the MRWA Code of Practice, **coordination of adjacent worksites is mandatory before approval** (Section 2, Page 20). You cannot unilaterally cover another worksite's signage – you must first coordinate with the other party and document the agreement in both TMPs. question: As a traffic controller what breaks am I meant to have
answer:
Based on **WHS Act 2020**, **WHS General Regulations 2022**, **MRWA WHS Control Standards**, **Construction Work COP**, and **MRWA COP May 2025**:

## Overview

There is no single "breaks rule" just for traffic controllers in Western Australian legislation. Instead, your break entitlements come from a combination of **WHS legislation** (which imposes a legal duty on your employer to manage fatigue risks), **MRWA mandatory standards** (which set work/rest cycles for thermal stress and fatigue), and **industry practice** from AGTTM. Your employer (the PCBU) must ensure you are not exposed to fatigue-related risks so far as reasonably practicable.

---

## 1. WHS Act 2020 — The Legal Foundation

### Section 19 — Primary Duty of Care

Your employer (PCBU) has a legal duty to ensure your health and safety, so far as reasonably practicable. This **includes managing fatigue**:

| Duty | What It Means for TCs |
|------|-----------------------|
| **Provide safe systems of work** | Work schedules that do not cause fatigue |
| **Monitor worker health** | Supervisors must watch for signs of fatigue |
| **Provide information and training** | You must be told about fatigue risks |
| **Maintain safe workplaces** | Rest facilities, shade, hydration must be provided |

### Section 84 — Right to Cease Unsafe Work

If you believe continuing to work would expose you to a **serious risk to health or safety from an immediate or imminent hazard** (including extreme fatigue or heat stress), you have the right to cease or refuse to carry out the work.

> **Key point:** You cannot be penalised for refusing unsafe work due to fatigue or heat stress. Your employer must find an alternative arrangement.

---

## 2. WHS General Regulations 2022 — Specific Requirements

### Regulation 40 — General Workplace Facilities

Your employer must provide **adequate workplace facilities**, including:

| Facility | Relevance to TCs |
|----------|------------------|
| **Rest areas** | Shade or sheltered area away from traffic for breaks |
| **Drinking water** | Must be readily accessible (not in a vehicle 100m away) |
| **Toilets** | Must be accessible within reasonable distance |
| **Seating** | Regulation 41B requires adequate seating when work can be done seated; for standing TCs, seating must be available for rest breaks |
| **Washing facilities** | For hot/unsealed work environments |

### Regulation 41A — Protection from Extremes of Heat and Cold

When working in extreme temperatures, the PCBU must:

| Requirement | Application |
|-------------|-------------|
| **Implement controls** | Shade, ventilation, cooling, rest schedules |
| **Monitor conditions** | Temperature monitoring, WBGT index if needed |
| **Modify work** | Adjust work/rest cycles based on conditions |

### Regulation 48 — Remote or Isolated Work

Traffic controllers often work as remote/isolated workers. The PCBU must provide:

| Control | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Effective communication** | Radio, phone, or other means to contact help |
| **Buddy system** | Not left alone for extended periods where feasible |
| **Emergency procedures** | Clear plan for medical or safety emergencies |

---

## 3. MRWA WHS Control Standards — Section 17: Exposure to Thermal Stress

This is the **most directly applicable standard** for traffic controller breaks in WA. It is **mandatory** under MRWA contracts.

### Section 17.2 — Hydration Management

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Water availability** | Cool, clean drinking water must be readily accessible |
| **Consumption encouraged** | Workers should drink 250mL every 15-20 minutes in heat |
| **No restriction** | Access to water must not be limited or delayed |

### Section 17.3 — Worker Acclimatisation

| Factor | Consideration |
|--------|---------------|
| **New workers** | Need 7-14 days to acclimatise to hot conditions |
| **Returning from leave** | Re-acclimatisation required |
| **Unacclimatised workers** | Shorter work periods, more frequent rest breaks |

### Section 17.4 — Work Task Management (Work/Rest Cycles)

This section sets the **work/rest regimes** based on thermal conditions:

| Heat Stress Level | Work/Rest Regime |
|-------------------|------------------|
| **Low risk** (WBGT < 25°C) | Normal schedule with regular rest breaks |
| **Moderate risk** (WBGT 25-28°C) | 50 min work / 10 min rest per hour |
| **High risk** (WBGT 28-30°C) | 40 min work / 20 min rest per hour |
| **Very high risk** (WBGT 30-32°C) | 30 min work / 30 min rest per hour |
| **Extreme risk** (WBGT > 32°C) | **Stop work** — only essential tasks with full controls |

> **Important:** These are MINIMUM standards under MRWA contracts. Your employer may apply more generous break schedules.

### Section 17.5 — Safe Work Practices in Hot Environments

| Practice | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|
| **Schedule heavy work** | For cooler parts of the day (early morning, late afternoon) |
| **Self-paced work** | Workers should not be pushed beyond comfortable pace |
| **Buddy system** | Workers watch each other for signs of heat stress |
| **Rest in shade** | Breaks must be taken in shaded or air-conditioned area |
| **Monitor for symptoms** | Cramps, exhaustion, dizziness, confusion |

---

## 4. Construction Work COP — Rest Break Requirements

Under the Construction Work Code of Practice (which applies to road construction work):

| Break Type | Minimum Entitlement |
|------------|---------------------|
| **Meal break** | 30 minutes after no more than 5 hours of continuous work |
| **Rest breaks** | As determined by risk assessment — more frequent in hot weather, heavy work, or long shifts |
| **Cooling breaks** | Additional breaks for heat stress as per thermal stress management |

---

## 5. AGTTM Part 7 — Traffic Controller Fitness for Duty

### Section 2.3 — Fitness for Duty

AGTTM Part 7 (Traffic Controllers) requires that traffic controllers be **fit for duty**. This means:

| Factor | Requirement |
|--------|-------------|
| **Fatigue** | TCs must not be impaired by fatigue when controlling traffic |
| **Rest periods** | Adequate rest must be provided between shifts |
| **Shift length** | Should not exceed safe working limits |
| **Supervision** | Supervisors must monitor TC fatigue levels |
| **Relief** | Arrangements for TC relief must be in place |

---

## 6. Practical Break Guide for Traffic Controllers

### Standard Shift Breaks

| Break Type | Duration | When |
|------------|----------|------|
| **Smoko / morning tea** | 10-15 minutes | Mid-morning (approx. 3 hours after start) |
| **Meal break / lunch** | 30 minutes | No later than 5 hours after shift start |
| **Smoko / afternoon tea** | 10-15 minutes | Mid-afternoon |
| **Rest breaks** | As needed | Additional breaks based on conditions |

### Adjustments for Conditions

| Condition | Additional Breaks |
|-----------|-------------------|
| **Hot weather (>30°C)** | 20-30 min rest per hour (MRWA WHS Controls Section 17.4) |
| **High traffic volume** | More frequent rotation between positions |
| **Night work** | Additional rest for circadian rhythm disruption |
| **Extended shift (>10 hours)** | Additional meal break and rest periods |
| **Remote location** | Ensure adequate relief TC available |

### Typical TC Rotation Pattern

On a standard day shift with two TCs:

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 06:00 - 08:30 | TC1 on position, TC2 standby/support |
| 08:30 - 09:00 | **Smoko break** — both TCs off position if possible |
| 09:00 - 11:30 | TC2 on position, TC1 standby/support |
| 11:30 - 12:00 | **Lunch break** — both TCs off position |
| 12:00 - 14:30 | TC1 on position, TC2 standby/support |
| 14:30 - 15:00 | **Smoko break** |
| 15:00 - 17:00 | TC2 on position, TC1 standby/support |

> **Note:** If only one TC is on site, relief must be arranged for meal and rest breaks. A TC must NOT leave their position unattended — cover must be arranged first.

---

## 7. What If I'm Not Getting Breaks?

### Your Rights

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| **1. Raise it** | Speak to your supervisor or site manager |
| **2. WHS concern** | Raise a WHS issue with your HSR (Health and Safety Representative) if you have one |
| **3. Cease unsafe work** | Under WHS Act Section 84, you can refuse to continue if fatigue creates a serious risk |
| **4. Report** | Contact WorkSafe WA if the issue is not resolved |

### Penalties for Employers

| Offence | Maximum Penalty |
|---------|-----------------|
| **Breach of WHS duty** | Individual: up to ,000 / Body corporate: up to 5,000 |
| **Reckless conduct** | Individual: up to 50,000 or 5 years jail / Body corporate: up to ,750,000 |

---

## Summary

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **What breaks am I entitled to?** | Smoko (10-15 min morning/afternoon), 30 min meal break within 5 hours, plus additional rest based on conditions |
| **What if it's hot?** | Work/rest cycles per MRWA WHS Controls Section 17.4 — up to 30 min rest per hour in extreme heat |
| **Can I refuse to work if fatigued?** | **Yes** — WHS Act Section 84 gives you the right to cease unsafe work |
| **Who decides break frequency?** | Your employer (PCBU) must assess risk and provide adequate breaks — it is a legal duty, not discretionary |
| **What facilities must be provided?** | Shade, water, seating, toilet access per WHS Regulations 40-41B |
| **Is there a set rule like "every 2 hours"?** | No fixed interval in WA legislation, but MRWA WHS thermal stress work/rest cycles and Construction COP meal break rules set minimum standards |

> **Key Rule:** Your employer has a legal duty under the WHS Act 2020 to manage fatigue risks. You are entitled to regular rest breaks, meal breaks, shade, water, and facilities. In hot conditions, MRWA WHS Control Standards Section 17 mandates specific work/rest cycles. If breaks are not being provided, you have the right to raise the issue and, if necessary, cease unsafe work.

question: As a traffic controller, what breaks am I meant to have?
answer:
Based on **AGTTM Part 7** (Traffic Controllers, Edition 1.1, 2021), **WHS General Regulations 2022**, and **MRWA WHS Control Standards**:

## Mandatory TC Breaks (AGTTM Part 7, Section 2.4.7)

### 15-Minute Break Every 2 Hours of Continuous STOP/SLOW Duty

Where having to stand at a station continuously for more than **2 hours**, traffic controllers **must be relieved** from their duty after not more than 2 hours for a period of rest or "other duties" of **at least 15 minutes**.

---

### What Counts as a Break

| Activity | Counts as a Break? |
|----------|--------------------|
| **Sitting down away from the bat** | YES |
| **Loading/unloading signs and equipment** | YES |
| **Setting up or removing temporary signs** | YES |
| **Driving between sites** | YES |
| **Operating a STOP/SLOW bat** | NO |
| **Operating a manual PTCD to control traffic** | NO |
| **Standing still in one position controlling traffic** | NO |
| **Being the lead TC at an intersection directing other TCs** | NO |

### The Intent of the Break

AGTTM Part 7 specifies two purposes for the break:

1. **Physical break** – from operating the STOP/SLOW bat (not from all traffic control duties)
2. **Mental break** – from perpetual STOP/SLOW activity, particularly in multi-traffic control or heavy traffic volume situations, to reduce the likelihood of traffic controller error

---

## Physical Capability Requirement (Section 2.3.4)

TCs must be capable of:

- Giving approved traffic control signals whilst **standing and holding a STOP/SLOW bat for periods of up to two continuous hours**
- **Concentrating and maintaining focus for entire work periods between rest breaks**

---

## Fatigue Management (Section 2.3.8)

| Requirement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **Fatigue prohibition** | TCs must NOT perform traffic control duties while suffering from fatigue that could impair their ability |
| **Heat exhaustion** | Must not perform duties while suffering fatigue associated with heat exhaustion |
| **Travel time** | Fatigue management includes consideration of time travelling to and from the worksite |
| **Work arrangements** | Number of shifts, breaks between shifts, and travel must comply with relevant jurisdictional legislation |

---

## Third TC Requirement (Section 2.9.9)

A **third traffic controller** is required when it is evident that continuous STOP/SLOW traffic controlling is required and **a break is needed**. This ensures that one TC can rotate off for a break while the other two maintain traffic control.

---

## Pre-Start Meeting (Section 2.7.2)

Breaks (e.g. toilet, water) **must be discussed** as part of the pre-start meeting before commencing traffic control duties.

---

## Thermal Stress and Hot Weather (MRWA WHS Controls, Section 17)

### Additional Break Considerations in Hot Conditions

| Control | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Hydration management** | Adequate fluids and refreshments must be available on site |
| **Work task management** | Task rotation and rest scheduling for heat stress |
| **Safe work practices** | Specific break schedules for hot environments |
| **Worker acclimatisation** | Gradual exposure for workers not used to heat |
| **Cooling packs** | Thermoregulation devices may be prepared in advance |

### WHS General Regulations 2022, Regulation 41A

The PCBU has a **duty to protect workers from extremes of heat and cold**. This includes providing adequate rest breaks in hot conditions beyond the standard 15-minute break.

---

## Longer Rest/Meal Breaks

AGTTM Part 7 states that **longer rest and meal breaks** are dealt with in accordance with:

- **Relevant industry awards** (e.g. Building and Construction General On-site Award)
- **Industrial agreements** (enterprise bargaining agreements)
- **WHS legislation** (WHS Act 2020, WHS General Regulations 2022)

Under typical WA industrial arrangements:

| Break Type | Typical Entitlement |
|------------|-------------------|
| **Meal break** | 30 minutes unpaid after 5 hours of work |
| **Rest break** | 10 minutes paid per 4 hours worked |
| **Maximum shift** | Varies by award/agreement (commonly 8-12 hours ordinary time) |

> **Important:** Your specific meal and rest break entitlements depend on your employment contract, applicable award, or enterprise agreement. Check with your employer for the exact breaks you are entitled to.

---

## Summary

| Break Type | Frequency | Duration | Source |
|------------|-----------|----------|--------|
| **STOP/SLOW relief break** | Every 2 hours of continuous bat duty | Minimum 15 minutes | AGTTM Part 7, Section 2.4.7 |
| **Paid rest break** | Per 4 hours worked | Typically 10 minutes | Industry award/agreement |
| **Unpaid meal break** | After 5 hours | Typically 30 minutes | Industry award/agreement |
| **Heat stress breaks** | As conditions require | As determined by risk assessment | MRWA WHS Controls, Section 17 |

> **Key Rule:** You must be relieved from STOP/SLOW bat duty for at least 15 minutes after every 2 hours of continuous operation. This is not optional – it is a mandatory safety requirement under AGTTM Part 7. Longer meal and rest breaks are governed by your applicable industry award or agreement.
